summary: Describes the leaptofrogans URI scheme, which lets applications launch Frogans Player on a given Frogans site. Frogans is a medium for publishing content and services, and Frogans Player is the software to browse Frogans sites. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A special link type that, when you click it, opens a particular viewer program to show a particular site.

questions: uri scheme to launch frogans player
how do i encode frogans addresses
subtitle: A URI scheme to launch Frogans Player on a specific site.

tldr.problem: Web pages and email messages need a way to let users launch Frogans Player on a given Frogans site, similar to how they can open a web browser or email client using URIs.
tldr.mechanism: The leaptofrogans URI scheme uses a Frogans address encoded as a percent-encoded Unicode string to identify which Frogans site to open, following the pattern leaptofrogans: followed by the encoded address.
tldr.outcome: Applications can now include links that launch Frogans Player, making Frogans a peer medium to the Web and email on the Internet.

today: RFC 8589 is an Informational RFC published in May 2019. The leaptofrogans URI scheme is registered as a permanent scheme with IANA and is used by Frogans Player and other applications to launch Frogans sites.

sections.title: About Frogans
sections.content:
Frogans is a medium for publishing content and services on the Internet alongside the World Wide Web. Designed since 1999 as a generic software layer on top of the TCP/IP protocols and DNS, Frogans sites differ from Web sites in emphasizing visual communication, focused content, and natural interaction over text and links.

Frogans technology includes the Frogans Slide Description Language (an XML-based format), Frogans addresses (international identifiers for accessing sites), Frogans Player (the browsing software), and the Frogans Core Registry (which resolves addresses). The OP3FT (Organization for the Promotion, Protection, and Progress of Frogans Technology) is a non-profit that develops and maintains these standards.
sections.plainLanguage: Frogans is another way to publish things on the Internet, like the Web but designed for visual and focused content. Frogans Player is the software to view Frogans sites.

sections.title: The Need for a URI Scheme
sections.content:
Just as Frogans sites can include links that launch a Web browser (using http: or https:) or an email client (using mailto:), users should be able to click links in Web pages and email messages to launch Frogans Player on a specific Frogans site.

Earlier attempts used a media type called vnd.frogans.ltf, but this approach required creating and hosting .ltf files on web servers, and it did not work reliably on mobile devices. A dedicated URI scheme is simpler and more direct.
sections.plainLanguage: If you see a link to a Frogans site in a Web page or email, you need a simple way to open it in Frogans Player, just like clicking a link opens your web browser.

sections.title: Scheme Syntax and Encoding
sections.content:
The leaptofrogans URI scheme encodes a Frogans address using the pattern leaptofrogans: followed by the address. Since Frogans addresses can contain Unicode characters (like Chinese or Arabic text), the scheme encodes non-ASCII characters using percent-encoding: each character is converted to UTF-8 bytes, then each byte is written as %HH where HH is the hex value.

For example, the ASCII Frogans address Network-Name*Site-Name becomes leaptofrogans:Network-Name*Site-Name, while a Chinese Frogans address with the same meaning becomes leaptofrogans:%E7%BD%91%E7%BB%9C%E5%90%8D*%E7%AB%99%E5%90%8D.

The scheme also supports Internationalized Resource Identifiers (IRIs), where the address is written directly in Unicode by omitting the percent-encoding. Frogans Player interprets both forms.
sections.plainLanguage: The link follows the pattern leaptofrogans: followed by the Frogans site address. Special characters are written as %HH codes so they work in regular links.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
A link's visible text can hide its true destination, a problem shared with web links. Frogans Player mitigates this by always displaying the actual Frogans address in the header before opening the site and requiring the user to confirm the action.

If an application provides an invalid Frogans address, Frogans Player validates it against the International Frogans Address Pattern (IFAP) specification and shows an error rather than attempting to open it.
sections.plainLanguage: Frogans Player shows you the real address before opening it and asks you to say yes, so you cannot be tricked by a misleading link.
